title: Cartridge-based flavored water bottles may pose a risk of developing dental erosion
html: The flavored water market has grown rapidly in the past several years, reflecting increasing consumer interest in drinking healthier beverages.1 In 2022, the global flavored water market was valued at approximately $15.97 billion, with projections estimating market expansion to $37.65 billion by 2031.1 This growth is driven by means of rising health awareness, concerns about sugar intake, and the demand for beverages enriched with vitamins, minerals, and natural ingredients.1 Among the products contributing to this market expansion, flavored water bottles (FWBs) with integrated suction-activated flavor cartridges (eg, Cirkul; Cirkul, Inc)2 or flavor delivery systems (eg, Selah; Selah Beverages, Inc and Air Up; Air Up Inc)3,4 have gained popularity among adolescents and young adults on social media.
